newsitem.title: USA: DEP emerges from Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: DEP emerges from Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

text.p: DEP Corp said on Monday it emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy under a plan approved by bankruptcy court on October 11.

Shares of DEP, a maker of hair, oral and skin-care products, will now trade on the Nasdaq SmallCap market under the symbol DEPC. The company has slightly less than 6.8 million common shares, including about 542,500 issued to lenders.
Under the plan, DEP has obtained $62 million in long-term financing at an interest rate of prime plus two percentage points. The debt matures on July 31, 2002.
In addition to 542,500 common shares, the lender group will receive $150,000 in cash to satisfy post-petition expenses and warrants to acquire about 330,000 more shares.
DEP will also assume about $1.15 million in post-bankruptcy professional fees and expenses incurred by lenders, less payments made while the company was in Chapter 11.
Monthly payments to the unsecured creditors will begin promptly, at 5 percent interest, and continue for the next 18 months, the company said.
